classification.difficultyReason: Form each composite, apply square-root or denominator restrictions to its domain, and determine its range, distinguishing the attained maximum of 1/(x²+1) from the excluded lower endpoint of 1/x²+1.

content.prompt: Find the domain and range of the composite functions $f(g(x))$ and $g(f(x))$ given that:

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f(g(x))&=f(\sqrt{x})\\f(g(x))&=\sqrt{x}-1.\end{align*}$$
The square root requires $x\geq0$. Since $\sqrt{x}\geq0$, the range is $y\geq-1$.
$$\begin{align*}g(f(x))&=g(x-1)\\g(f(x))&=\sqrt{x-1}.\end{align*}$$
Here $x-1\geq0$, so the domain is $x\geq1$. The square root takes every nonnegative value, so the range is $y\geq0$.

$$\begin{align*}f(g(x))&=f(x^2+1)\\f(g(x))&=\frac{1}{x^2+1}.\end{align*}$$
Since $x^2+1\geq1$, the denominator is never zero. The domain is all real $x$ and the range is $0<y\leq1$; the maximum $1$ occurs at $x=0$.
$$\begin{align*}g(f(x))&=g\left(\frac1x\right)\\g(f(x))&=\frac{1}{x^2}+1.\end{align*}$$
The inner function requires $x\ne0$, so the domain is $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$. For these inputs, $\frac{1}{x^2}$ takes every positive value, giving range $y>1$.
